name: Grant Tran
life: “I still remember the evening an audience member asked me to leave the camera shut.” Wednesday often includes a stop at Studio Boulevard, where Grant waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I usually photograph every performance. I put the camera away because the mother wanted her face to be private.
appearance: Grant has thick, tightly coiled hair, a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a faded indigo overshirt. It usually goes with a train token tied to a zipper pull. When somebody else has the floor, Grant steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Grant enjoys routines and will defend the right of someone else to break one. As a result, Grant is often everyone's favorite cover for a missed morning.
agenda: To take no unauthorized picture of the mother.
family: Max Clay is Grant’s half-sibling. Grant asks the question the rest of the family avoided. Max chooses an ordinary story to tell. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *The housecoat commission*, Max says, “I bought washable cloth and lied about the price.”
connections: Yvette Hill. A donor funding one more hour backs the photographer's choice to let the occasion stay private.

reactions.situation: The working parent arrives after the curtain time
reactions.response: Grant waits for the parent to be seated before asking the cast to start.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Grant asks everybody to retrace their own last ordinary actions before asking the young worker a question.

reactions.situation: If a family plan changes at the door
reactions.response: Grant keeps a place for the late person without making the others postpone their meal.
